issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor drops outer Delimited, regressing support for comma-chained multi-action ALTER statements.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this. The prior grammar wrapped the OneOf in Delimited(...), accepting valid T-SQL like `ALTER TABLE t ADD col ..., DROP COLUMN x`. The PR replaces this with a single OneOf, silently disallowing mixed ADD/DROP/ALTER actions in one statement. Either restore the outer Delimited or explicitly document and justify the scope reduction in the commit message.

issues.description: A passing fixture proving mixed ADD/DROP ALTER TABLE syntax was deleted without replacement or justification.
issues.detail: All three reviewers note the removed example `ADD column_b ... CONSTRAINT exb_unique UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c` is documented MSDN syntax. Deleting a load-bearing passing fixture to make a refactor pass is the tell for a silent regression. Either restore the fixture (and the grammar that parses it) or cite proof it was invalid T-SQL.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar accepts SignedSegmentGrammar on the increment without constraint or test coverage.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this. The optional sign now precedes both seed and increment numerics; T-SQL constrains increment to a non-zero signed value, but the grammar permits oddities like `(+1, -0)`. Either tighten the grammar (or model a SignedNumericLiteral value), or add fixtures for negative increment and document the looseness as intentional.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE widened to accept NumericLiteralSegment without citation or test coverage.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag the unjustified expansion. CREATE LOGIN's DEFAULT_LANGUAGE takes a language name or lcid alias per MS docs, not arbitrary numeric literals at this grammar position. Either cite the lcid case and add a fixture exercising the numeric path, or drop the NumericLiteralSegment alternative entirely.

issues.description: Four unrelated grammar changes shipped as one patch, hurting bisectability and review.
issues.detail: Table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN identifiers, signed IDENTITY seed, and ALTER TABLE DROP refactor are independent features touching different segments. They should land as separate diffs so each can be reverted, bisected, or refused on its own merits. The ALTER TABLE rewrite in particular deserves isolation given its regression risk.

issues.description: New fixtures cover only happy paths; boundary cases and the common DROP COLUMN shape are untested.
issues.detail: Missing fixtures: IDENTITY with positive sign or zero increment, CREATE LOGIN with numeric DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, and the canonical `DROP COLUMN a, b, c` shape (one COLUMN keyword, delimited refs). The new fixture only exercises the redundant `DROP COLUMN a, COLUMN b` form. Without negative and boundary cases, the grammar's actual surface is unverified.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches strong consensus: NEEDS-WORK. The ALTER TABLE refactor silently regresses comma-chained multi-action syntax by removing the outer Delimited wrapper, and the deleted fixture that proved this worked is documented MSDN syntax. The IDENTITY signed-seed change is over-permissive (sign on increment) and untested at boundaries. DEFAULT_LANGUAGE was widened to accept numeric literals without citation or test. Compounding these, four independent grammar changes were bundled into one patch with happy-path-only fixtures. Recommend splitting the patch, restoring or justifying the ALTER TABLE behavior change, tightening IDENTITY, and adding boundary fixtures.
